```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      cache = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
```

# Purpose

The Stage 1 bagging result was far worse than a single CART tree and even worse
than the store-mean baseline, which should not happen if bagging is implemented
correctly. This file is fully self-contained (no `source()`): it loads the data,
builds the same features and split as Stage 1, and instruments the bagging model
so the cause is visible. It grows deep trees, reports train, out-of-bag, and test
error, and sweeps the two settings that decide whether bagging behaves: the
number of features each split may use (`mtry`) and the minimum terminal-node
size.

# 1. Packages and configuration

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ranger)
library(rpart)

TRAIN_CSV <- "train.csv"
STORE_CSV <- "store.csv"
TEST_DAYS <- 42
SEED      <- 42
N_THREADS <- max(1L, parallel::detectCores() - 1L)
set.seed(SEED)
```

# 2. Data loading and preprocessing (same as Stage 1)

```{r load}
train_raw <- read_csv(TRAIN_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))
store_raw <- read_csv(STORE_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE)

df <- train_raw %>%
  filter(Open == 1, Sales > 0) %>%
  left_join(store_raw, by = "Store") %>%
  mutate(
    Year = year(Date), Month = month(Date), Week = isoweek(Date),
    DayOfMonth = mday(Date), Quarter = quarter(Date),
    IsWeekend = as.integer(DayOfWeek %in% c(6, 7)),
    StateHoliday = case_when(StateHoliday == "a" ~ 1L, StateHoliday == "b" ~ 2L,
                             StateHoliday == "c" ~ 3L, TRUE ~ 0L),
    CompetitionOpenMonths = ifelse(
      !is.na(CompetitionOpenSinceYear) & !is.na(CompetitionOpenSinceMonth),
      (Year - CompetitionOpenSinceYear) * 12 + (Month - CompetitionOpenSinceMonth),
      NA_real_),
    CompetitionOpenMonths = pmax(CompetitionOpenMonths, 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    StoreType  = as.integer(factor(StoreType,  levels = c("a", "b", "c", "d"))),
    Assortment = as.integer(factor(Assortment, levels = c("a", "b", "c")))
  ) %>%
  select(Store, Date, Sales, DayOfWeek, Promo, StateHoliday, SchoolHoliday,
         StoreType, Assortment, CompetitionDistance, Promo2,
         Year, Month, Week, DayOfMonth, Quarter, IsWeekend, CompetitionOpenMonths)

med_comp <- median(df$CompetitionDistance, na.rm = TRUE)
df <- df %>%
  mutate(CompetitionDistance   = replace_na(CompetitionDistance, med_comp),
         CompetitionOpenMonths = replace_na(CompetitionOpenMonths, 0)) %>%
  arrange(Date, Store)

FEAT_S1 <- c("Store", "DayOfWeek", "Promo", "StateHoliday", "SchoolHoliday",
             "StoreType", "Assortment", "CompetitionDistance", "Promo2",
             "Year", "Month", "Week", "DayOfMonth", "Quarter", "IsWeekend",
             "CompetitionOpenMonths")
cat("Rows:", nrow(df), "| Stores:", n_distinct(df$Store), "\n")
```

```{r split}
split_data <- function(data, feature_cols, test_days = TEST_DAYS) {
  data   <- data %>% arrange(Date, Store)
  dates  <- sort(unique(data$Date))
  cutoff <- dates[length(dates) - test_days]
  train  <- data %>% filter(Date <= cutoff)
  test   <- data %>% filter(Date >  cutoff)
  list(X_train = as.matrix(train[, feature_cols]), y_train = train$Sales,
       X_test  = as.matrix(test[, feature_cols]),  y_test  = test$Sales,
       train = train, test = test)
}
sp <- split_data(df, FEAT_S1)
p  <- ncol(sp$X_train)
cat("Train rows:", length(sp$y_train), "| Test rows:", length(sp$y_test),
    "| Features p =", p, "\n")
```

```{r metrics}
eval_metrics <- function(actual, pred) {
  v <- !is.na(actual) & actual != 0
  tibble(RMSE = sqrt(mean((actual - pred)^2)),
         MAE  = mean(abs(actual - pred)),
         MAPE = mean(abs((actual[v] - pred[v]) / actual[v])) * 100)
}
delta_rel <- function(ref, x) (ref - x) / ref * 100
```

# 3. Reference points

The bagging numbers below only make sense next to the models around them: the two
naive baselines, a single deep CART tree, and a random forest (which is bagging
*with* feature subsampling). A correct bagging should land between the single
tree and the random forest, not behind the baselines.

```{r references}
# store-mean and store-DOW baselines from the training data
sm  <- sp$train %>% group_by(Store) %>% summarise(mu = mean(Sales), .groups = "drop")
gm  <- mean(sp$train$Sales)
dow <- sp$train %>% group_by(Store, DayOfWeek) %>% summarise(md = mean(Sales), .groups = "drop")
pred_mean <- sp$test %>% left_join(sm, by = "Store") %>% mutate(p = coalesce(mu, gm)) %>% pull(p)
pred_dow  <- sp$test %>% left_join(dow, by = c("Store", "DayOfWeek")) %>%
  left_join(sm, by = "Store") %>% mutate(p = coalesce(md, mu, gm)) %>% pull(p)

df_tr <- as.data.frame(sp$X_train); df_tr$Sales <- sp$y_train
df_te <- as.data.frame(sp$X_test)

cart <- rpart(Sales ~ ., df_tr, control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 20, cp = 1e-5, minsplit = 10))
rf   <- ranger(Sales ~ ., df_tr, num.trees = 200, num.threads = N_THREADS,
               seed = SEED, verbose = FALSE)

ref <- bind_rows(
  eval_metrics(sp$y_test, pred_mean) %>% mutate(Model = "Store-mean baseline"),
  eval_metrics(sp$y_test, pred_dow)  %>% mutate(Model = "Store-DOW baseline"),
  eval_metrics(sp$y_test, predict(cart, df_te)) %>% mutate(Model = "CART (single tree)"),
  eval_metrics(sp$y_test, predict(rf, df_te)$predictions) %>% mutate(Model = "Random Forest (mtry = sqrt p)")
) %>% select(Model, RMSE, MAE, MAPE) %>% mutate(across(RMSE:MAE, round))
ref
rmse_mean <- ref$RMSE[ref$Model == "Store-mean baseline"]
```

# 4. Bagging: a deep, instrumented implementation

```{r run-bagging-fn}
# Bagging averages many low-bias, high-variance trees grown on bootstrap samples.
# Trees are grown deep (max.depth = 0 = unlimited). With mtry = p every split may
# use all predictors, which is what distinguishes bagging from a random forest.
run_bagging <- function(sp, B = 200, mtry = NULL, min_node_size = 5,
                        max_depth = 0, verbose = TRUE) {
  tr <- as.data.frame(sp$X_train); tr$Sales <- sp$y_train
  te <- as.data.frame(sp$X_test)
  if (is.null(mtry)) mtry <- ncol(sp$X_train)
  fit <- ranger(Sales ~ ., data = tr, num.trees = B, mtry = mtry,
                min.node.size = min_node_size, max.depth = max_depth,
                replace = TRUE, sample.fraction = 1,
                num.threads = N_THREADS, seed = SEED, verbose = FALSE)
  pred_te <- predict(fit, te)$predictions
  if (verbose) {
    pred_tr <- predict(fit, tr)$predictions
    cat(sprintf("  bagging[B=%d, mtry=%d, min.node=%d]  train %.0f | OOB %.0f | test %.0f\n",
                B, mtry, min_node_size,
                sqrt(mean((sp$y_train - pred_tr)^2)),
                sqrt(fit$prediction.error),
                sqrt(mean((sp$y_test  - pred_te)^2))))
  }
  eval_metrics(sp$y_test, pred_te)
}
```

```{r bagging-textbook}
# Textbook bagging: mtry = p, deep trees, B = 200.
set.seed(SEED)
bag_textbook <- run_bagging(sp, B = 200, mtry = p, min_node_size = 5)
bag_textbook %>% mutate(Model = "Bagging (mtry = p, deep)", .before = 1)
```

A small train RMSE next to a much larger test RMSE means the trees fit the
training period and fail to carry to the held-out future window, the failure mode
that feature subsampling in a random forest avoids.

# 5. Sensitivity sweep

```{r sweep}
grid <- expand_grid(mtry          = c(p, round(p/2), floor(sqrt(p)), max(1, floor(p/3))),
                    min_node_size = c(5, 20, 50))
sweep <- pmap_dfr(grid, function(mtry, min_node_size) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  fit <- ranger(Sales ~ ., data = df_tr, num.trees = 200, mtry = mtry,
                min.node.size = min_node_size, max.depth = 0,
                replace = TRUE, sample.fraction = 1,
                num.threads = N_THREADS, seed = SEED, verbose = FALSE)
  pr_tr <- predict(fit, df_tr)$predictions
  pr_te <- predict(fit, df_te)$predictions
  tibble(mtry = mtry, min_node_size = min_node_size,
         train_RMSE = round(sqrt(mean((sp$y_train - pr_tr)^2))),
         OOB_RMSE   = round(sqrt(fit$prediction.error)),
         test_RMSE  = round(sqrt(mean((sp$y_test - pr_te)^2))),
         vs_mean    = round(delta_rel(rmse_mean, sqrt(mean((sp$y_test - pr_te)^2))), 1))
}) %>% arrange(test_RMSE)
sweep
```

If lowering `mtry` below `p`, or raising the minimum node size, pulls the test
RMSE into the random-forest range, the original poor number was a decorrelation
and overfitting problem rather than a coding mistake, and the reported bagging
specification can be set to the configuration that behaves sensibly.

# 6. Bagging and random forest as canonical configurations

Bagging and the random forest are the same bootstrap-averaged ensemble at
different `mtry`. This chunk reports the three standard choices with full
metrics, all with `B = 200` deep trees and `min.node.size = 5`, so the Stage 1
table can use fair, properly configured numbers for both:

- Random forest, ranger default `mtry = floor(sqrt(p))` (the classification default);
- Random forest, regression default `mtry = floor(p/3)`;
- Bagging, `mtry = p`.

```{r named-configs}
rmse_dow <- ref$RMSE[ref$Model == "Store-DOW baseline"]
ens_fit <- function(mtry) {
  set.seed(SEED)
  fit <- ranger(Sales ~ ., data = df_tr, num.trees = 200, mtry = mtry,
                min.node.size = 5, max.depth = 0, replace = TRUE,
                sample.fraction = 1, num.threads = N_THREADS, seed = SEED, verbose = FALSE)
  eval_metrics(sp$y_test, predict(fit, df_te)$predictions) %>% mutate(mtry = mtry)
}
configs <- bind_rows(
  ens_fit(floor(sqrt(p))) %>% mutate(Model = "Random Forest (mtry = sqrt p, default)"),
  ens_fit(floor(p/3))     %>% mutate(Model = "Random Forest (mtry = p/3, regression)"),
  ens_fit(p)              %>% mutate(Model = "Bagging (mtry = p)")
) %>%
  mutate(delta_mean = round(delta_rel(rmse_mean, RMSE), 1),
         delta_dow  = round(delta_rel(rmse_dow,  RMSE), 1),
         across(c(RMSE, MAE), round), MAPE = round(MAPE, 1)) %>%
  select(Model, mtry, RMSE, MAE, MAPE, delta_mean, delta_dow)
configs
dir.create("thesis_tables", showWarnings = FALSE)
# Written for the thesis: Table 11, random-forest row (mtry = p/3) and the
# mtry comparison quoted in README section 5.
write_csv(configs, "thesis_tables/bagging_rf_configs.csv")
write_csv(configs, "bagging_rf_configs.csv")
```

The row for `mtry = p/3` is the fair random-forest number to report in the thesis
(regression default), and `mtry = p` is bagging.
